newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola earnings jump 38 percent; stock gains.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola earnings jump 38 percent; stock gains.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co. Monday reported a 38 percent jump in first-quarter earnings, exceeding Wall Street's expectations and boosting the soft drink giant's stock.
The company said it earned $987 million, or 40 cents a share, on sales of $4.13 billion vs. earnings of $713 million, or 28 cents a share, on sales of $4.22 billion in the first quarter of last year.
Coca-Cola's stock gained $1.25 to $55 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The earnings surpassed analysts' estimates of about 38 cents a share.
The company said its first-quarter profits included a gain of 8 cents a share from the sale of its 49 percent stake in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages to Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc.
It said U.S. unit case volume increased 9 percent in the first quarter following an 8 percent rise in the first quarter of 1996.

"Our extremely strong first quarter unit case volume gain demonstrates the continuing power of our aligned global bottling system and is a solid start toward, once again, achieving our long term volume and EPS (estimated per share) growth objectives in 1997," said Roberto C. Goizueta, chairman and chief executive officer.
"We remain sharply focused on strengthening our system to capture the immense opportunities that exist around the world," he said.
Coca-Cola said its worldwide unit case volume grew 9 percent and gallon shipments of concentrates and syrups increased 7 percent, both exceeding expectations.
It said volume growth was strong across the United States.

"Results like this in our flagship market, coupled with share gains, demonstrate again that our U.S. business is far from being a mature market for soft drinks -- in fact, it is capable of dramatic growth," Goizueta. said.
